**What changed:** `@angular/compiler-cli` now reports host binding parser errors (diagnostic `HOST_BINDING_PARSE_ERROR = 5001`, e.g. a host binding/listener expression containing a pipe) against the individual property initializer inside the `host` object literal, instead of highlighting the whole `host` object literal. Previously all host binding source spans pointed at the root object literal, because the object is passed around as a `Record<string, string>` for JIT/non-JIT support and the AOT compiler evaluates the entire literal at once, making IDE output "very noisy" (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/fb1fa8b0fc04c9cfac6551ca27bee89dcd7c72ac, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58870). The improved span is produced "for the most common case where the `host` object is initialized to a `string -> string` object literal by matching the failing expression to one of the property initializers"; it is explicitly "not 100% reliable", since cases like `host: SOME_CONST` still cannot be mapped to a single property (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58870). No public API, decorator, or error-code surface changed — the codes and their docs are unchanged in `error_code.ts` (e.g. `HOST_BINDING_PARSE_ERROR = 5001` remains "Raised when a host expression has a parse error, such as a host listener or host binding expression containing a pipe").

**Affects:** applications with `@Component`/`@Directive` `host` metadata or `@HostBinding`/`@HostListener` expressions that fail to parse; only the location/text of the reported diagnostic changes, never whether one is reported.

**Action:** none — diagnostic quality only; re-verify that any tooling that parses compiler output by source span (custom lint/IDE integrations, tests asserting on error positions) still behaves as expected.

**Before/after:**
```ts
  /**
   * Raised when a host expression has a parse error, such as a host listener or host binding
   * expression containing a pipe.
   */
  HOST_BINDING_PARSE_ERROR = 5001,
```

**What changed:** Angular now explicitly calls a disposal callback to finalize a `TracingSnapshot` once it has been used, rather than leaving the snapshot to be implicitly released. The underlying tracing implementation may use reference counting and needs to release resources to enable the trace to complete. Previously, change detection used the snapshot for exactly one callback, but after-render hooks run multiple times in sequence; the fix provides a predictable way to indicate when the snapshot can be finalized. The PR notes that the current behavior failed because the experimental implementation attempted to run previously resumed snapshots; the new behavior has Angular explicitly call `dispose` to release refcounts. The PR is marked as a bugfix that does not introduce a breaking change (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58929, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/4792db9a6d3a7dc076c9b200cd31a53a4fd30683).

**Affects:** Applications that provide a custom implementation of Angular's experimental `TracingService` (tracing is experimental and not enabled in standard applications).

**Action:** unclear from the sources. The fetched commit and PR pages do not show the concrete API/property signatures changed in `TracingSnapshot`/`TracingService` (the tracing source files could not be located), so a specific code migration step cannot be cited. Re-verify any custom `TracingService` implementation still works with explicit snapshot disposal.

**What changed:** This is a bug fix inside the `ng generate @angular/core:inject` schematic (the `inject()` migration), not an application API change. In the migration code (`packages/core/schematics/ng-generate/inject-migration/migration.ts`), when a constructor's body after the `super(...)` call consisted only of statements that the migration deletes (e.g. property assignments replaced by `inject()` field initializers), previously inserted statements were written at `superCall.getEnd() + 1`, causing code to be dropped. The fix inserts at `constructor.getEnd() - 1` and adds `memberIndentation` when no preserved statement follows (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/4392ccedf997e79486af7ad60172eea98ed3351f, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58959). It was part of PR #58959 "Fixes for edge cases in inject migration" (also: class content deletion, comments around parameters, aggressive import removal, type literals/tuples, skipping uninjectable parameters), merged with `action: merge, target: patch, area: migrations` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58959).

**Affects:** Only projects that run the `inject` migration schematic on classes extending a base class where the derived constructor's post-`super` statements are all removed by the migration; no runtime or build behaviour of the upgraded app changes.

**Action:** none — if you run `ng generate @angular/core:inject`, re-verify the migrated files' diffs as usual; the fix improves the schematic's output correctness in Angular 20.

**Before/after:**
```typescript
// migration.ts (schematic internals)
-      nextStatement ? nextStatement.getFullStart() : superCall.getEnd() + 1,
-      `\n${afterSuper.join('\n')}\n`,
+      nextStatement ? nextStatement.getFullStart() : constructor.getEnd() - 1,
+      `\n${afterSuper.join('\n')}\n` + (nextStatement ? '' : memberIndentation),
```

**What changed:** In Angular 19.0, `@angular/platform-server` listed `@angular/animations` in its `peerDependencies`, but the package did not actually use it anywhere, so the entry was removed in v20 (commit f3c388ecda, PR #58997) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/f3c388ecda5e836946031a554827cdaee9801734). The diff only drops `"@angular/animations": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER"` from `packages/platform-server/package.json` `peerDependencies` and the `//packages/animations/browser` dep from `packages/platform-server/BUILD.bazel`; remaining peer deps in v20 are `@angular/common`, `@angular/compiler`, `@angular/core`, `@angular/platform-browser`, `rxjs` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.0.x/packages/platform-server/package.json, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/19.0.x/packages/platform-server/package.json).

**Affects:** Applications using `@angular/platform-server`; only the package metadata changed — no API, import or code surface of `@angular/platform-server` changed. Apps using animations still need `@angular/animations` for `@angular/platform-browser` / `@angular/platform-browser/animations`, so it should remain installed in those projects.

**Action:** none. npm/yarn/pnpm may no longer require `@angular/animations` to satisfy `@angular/platform-server`'s peer requirements; projects that use animations keep the dependency for other packages. No schematic or code change accompanies this commit.

**Before/after:**
```jsonc
// packages/platform-server/package.json — peerDependencies
// 19.0 (before)
"@angular/animations": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER",
"@angular/common": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER",
// 20.0 (after)
"@angular/common": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER",
```

Confirmed: 19.0.3 is an empty changelog section — a re-publish with no code changes. **What changed:** Nothing. The Angular v19.0.3 release (dated 2024-12-04, the same date as v19.0.2) consists of an empty changelog section: in both the `19.0.3` and `19.0.4` tags of `CHANGELOG.md`, the heading ` / # 19.0.3 (2024-12-04)` is immediately followed by `` with no `### ` sections or commit rows at all (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/19.0.3/CHANGELOG.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/19.0.4/CHANGELOG.md). The neighbouring 19.0.2 patch (same day) does list entries — `compiler-cli` "account for multiple generated namespace imports in HMR (#58924)", `core` "Explicitly manage TracingSnapshot lifecycle… (#58929)", six `migrations` fixes from #58959, and `platform-server` "remove peer dependency on animations (#58997)" — and the GitHub release page for `v19.0.3` likewise renders no release body (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/19.0.3). `@angular/core@19.0.3` was published to npm with the same 19.0.0 `ng-update` packageGroup and peerDependencies `rxjs: ^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0`, `zone.js: ~0.15.0`, i.e. no new API surface (npm registry metadata). This row is a changelog-anchor artifact of the hop's 19.x patch history, not a behavioral change. **Affects:** none — 19.0.3 introduced no code, API, dependency or configuration change relative to 19.0.2, so nothing in an upgrading application can be affected by it. **Action:** none

**What changed:** The row title "19.0.3 (2024-12-04)" does not appear in the 19.0 → 20.0 changelog as a migration-relevant behavioral change: it is a patch release of Angular 19.0.x. The only changelog entries dated 2024-12-04 are patch-release fix lists, not behavioral changes. The framework changelog at tag 19.0.3 shows a section "# 19.0.3 (2024-12-04)" with an empty body (only `<!-- CHANGELOG SPLIT MARKER -->`), and the CLI changelog at tag 19.0.3 lists only `fix` commits — e.g. @angular/cli "correctly select package versions in descending order during `ng add`", @angular/build "apply define option to JavaScript from scripts option", @angular/ssr "apply HTML transformation to CSR responses", @schematics/angular "add required type to `CanDeactivate` guard" — with no breaking-change or deprecation entries (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/19.0.3/CHANGELOG.md, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular-cli/19.0.3/CHANGELOG.md). The fetched 19.0.3 test-bed source shows no 19.0.3-specific behavioral change either.

**Affects:** none — upgrading applications migrating from 19.0.0 to 20.0.0 do nothing specifically because of the 19.0.3 patch release; its content is bug fixes within the 19.0 line.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```ts
// @angular/cli 19.0.3 fix, no code change required by applications
// "correctly select package versions in descending order during `ng add`"
```

**What changed:** The `compiler-cli` HMR dependency analyzer (`packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/hmr/src/extract_dependencies.ts`, `PotentialTopLevelReadsVisitor.isTopLevelIdentifierReference`) previously only recognised a few parent node kinds (e.g. `ts.isPropertyAccessExpression`, `ts.isClassDeclaration`) when deciding whether an identifier in a `WrappedNodeExpr` was a top-level read. It now also handles `ts.isComputedPropertyName`, `ts.isTemplateSpan`, `ts.isSpreadAssignment`, `ts.isSpreadElement`, `ts.isAwaitExpression`, `ts.isNonNullExpression`, `ts.isIfStatement`, `ts.isDoStatement`, `ts.isWhileStatement`, `ts.isForInStatement`, `ts.isForOfStatement`, `ts.isSwitchStatement`, `ts.isCaseClause`, `ts.isThrowStatement`, `ts.isFunctionDeclaration`, `ts.isVariableDeclaration`, `ts.isShorthandPropertyAssignment`, `ts.isElementAccessExpression`, `ts.isBinaryExpression`, `ts.isImportSpecifier` and `ts.isExportSpecifier` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/06a55e98173ff7bdd4e2ac1263309f9b935240f0.diff). Previously such identifiers were dropped from the captured local/external HMR dependencies, so the generated `ɵɵreplaceMetadata` call and `<Cmp>_UpdateMetadata` function were missing arguments/parameters — e.g. `@defer` dependencies producing a broken HMR update function (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59310).

**Affects:** Applications with HMR enabled (`ng serve --hmr` / `hmr` option) whose components reference top-level symbols (imports, consts, functions) in component metadata via expressions beyond plain property reads — e.g. shorthand properties (`providers`), spreads, `await`, binary/array/element-access expressions, or templates using `@defer`.

**Action:** none — internal compiler-cli bug fix; no code, config or dependency change needed. Re-verify that template/`@defer` HMR updates apply without console errors.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// test expectations added by the fix (hmr_spec.ts)
expect(jsContents).toContain(
  'ɵɵreplaceMetadata(Cmp, m.default, [i0], [providers, Component]));');
expect(hmrContents).toContain(
  'export default function Cmp_UpdateMetadata(Cmp, ɵɵnamespaces, providers, Component) {');
```

**What changed:** `AsyncAnimationRendererFactory` (in `@angular/platform-browser/animations/async`) previously injected `ChangeDetectionScheduler` eagerly via `inject(ChangeDetectionScheduler, {optional: true})`. This could cause a `NG0200: Circular dependency in DI detected` error when the factory was instantiated during app initialization—e.g. via a custom `ErrorHandler` that injects `RendererFactory2`/`Renderer2Factory`, which the CDK `Overlay` (and thus `MatSnackbar`) depends on (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59255). The fix in `async_animation_renderer.ts` removes the eager injection and instead injects `Injector`, resolving `ChangeDetectionScheduler` lazily only when the async animation renderer is loaded, via `this.injector.get(ChangeDetectionScheduler, null, {optional: true})` (https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/59256.diff, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/dbb8980d03485ad1cf0e19503c4e770b1ba0767e). This is an internal bug fix that removes the error rather than a new API; it is not listed in the 20.0.0 release notes' Breaking Changes section (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/20.0.0).

**Affects:** Applications using `provideAnimationsAsync()` together with code that injects `RendererFactory2`/`Renderer2` during app initialization, most commonly a custom `ErrorHandler` that uses `Overlay`/`MatSnackbar`.

**Action:** none. The change fixes the `Circular dependency in DI detected for ChangeDetectionScheduler` runtime error; applications need no code, configuration, or dependency change beyond upgrading to Angular 20.0.0. Re-verify that an app using `provideAnimationsAsync()` with an error handler injecting the renderer factory no longer throws the circular DI error.

**What changed:** Two-way (`[(...)]`) binding expressions are validated by `BindingParser` in `@angular/compiler` (`packages/compiler/src/template_parser/binding_parser.ts`), which historically only permitted property reads (`PropertyRead`, `KeyedRead`) and rejected anything else with e.g. `Parser Error: Unexpected token '=' at column 12 in [$any(name) =$event]` (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/51165). Angular 20 adds a case to the validation: a `Call` whose `receiver` is a `PropertyRead` named `$any` on an `ImplicitReceiver` (i.e. not `this.$any`) with exactly one argument is unwrapped via `this._isAllowedAssignmentEvent(ast.args[0])`, so `<input [(ngModel)]="$any(value)">` and `<div dir [(val)]="$any(invalidType)">` now compile and type-check, including with `strictTemplates` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59362, commit ceadd28ea12140e8e78cdb706aff0487f5a87a3c). Still rejected: `$any(a || b)`, `this.$any(a)`, `$any(a, b)` (test case list in the diff). Emits `ɵɵtwoWayProperty` / `ɵɵtwoWayListener` + `ɵɵtwoWayBindingSet` against the unwrapped target.

**Affects:** Templates that use `$any(...)` on the right-hand side of a two-way binding; such templates previously failed to compile in v19. No effect on other templates.

**Action:** none — purely a relaxation of template validation; no code, config or dependency changes required.

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- v19: parser error; v20: compiles and type-checks -->
<input [(ngModel)]="$any(value)">
<div dir [(val)]="$any(invalidType)">
```

**What changed:** The Angular compiler's generated HMR code (from `r3_hmr_compiler.ts`, used when template HMR is active) now builds the dynamically imported URL from `import.meta.url` instead of resolving it against the HTML base HREF. The generated code changed from `import(/* @vite-ignore */ "/@ng/component?c=test.ts%40Cmp&t=" + encodeURIComponent(t))` to `import(/* @vite-ignore */ new URL("/@ng/component?c=test.ts%40Cmp&t=" + encodeURIComponent(t), import.meta.url).href)`, so the `/@ng/component` HMR request is sent to the same origin that served the application chunk. This fixes setups where the HTML base HREF differs from the Angular dev server location (for example dev servers behind proxies or with a non-matching `<base href>`); the change was made in the compiler (PR #59459, commit aed49dd) and shipped in Angular 20.0.0 (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59459, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/aed49ddaaa40d6e6816198b47ceada4e98cd636c).

**Affects:** Applications using template/component HMR during development (`ng serve --hmr` workflow served via `@angular/build`/Vite, where the compiler emits the `Cmp_HmrLoad` function that fetches `/@ng/component?...`). No production code paths are affected; in most cases the base HREF already matches the code origin and behavior is unchanged (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/aed49ddaaa40d6e6816198b47ceada4e98cd636c).

**Action:** none — this is internal generated-code behavior; no application source, configuration, or dependency changes are required. Applications with a base HREF different from the dev server origin should re-verify that HMR template updates still work as expected.

**Before/after:**
```js
// Before (generated HMR code)
import(/* @vite-ignore */
  "/@ng/component?c=test.ts%40Cmp&t=" + encodeURIComponent(t))

// After (generated HMR code)
import(/* @vite-ignore */
  new URL("/@ng/component?c=test.ts%40Cmp&t=" + encodeURIComponent(t), import.meta.url).href)
```
(from the test diff in https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/aed49ddaaa40d6e6816198b47ceada4e98cd636c)

**What changed:** PR #58609 ("feat(core): support TypeScript 5.7") updated the Angular repository to allow TypeScript 5.7 to be used ((https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58609), (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/bd1f1294aeb0d47b24421b7b7a608988689a459f)). By the 20.0.0 release, the workspace devDependency in `package.json` was pinned to `typescript: "5.8.2"`, effectively replacing 5.7 (and prior) with 5.8 as the supported compiler ((https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.0.0/package.json)).

**Affects:** Applications declaring a TypeScript version below 5.8 in their `package.json` `devDependencies`.

**Action:** required: set the `typescript` devDependency to 5.8 (the release pins `typescript: "5.8.2"`); `@angular/core` 20.0.0 itself declares no TypeScript peer dependency, so no peer entry change is required ((https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.0.0/packages/core/package.json)).

**Before/after:**
```json
"devDependencies": {
-  "typescript": "5.7.x"
+  "typescript": "5.8.2"
}
```

**What changed:** The commit `14fb8ce4c0` ("fix(migrations): resolve text replacement issue (#59452)") fixes a bug in the `@angular/core:cleanup-unused-imports` schematic (added in v19 via `PR 59353`) that could cause code to be duplicated in some setups. The bug was that the schematic used `recorder.insertLeft(c.data.position, c.data.toInsert);` instead of `recorder.insertRight(...)` when removing unused imports from components' `imports` arrays ((https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/14fb8ce4c00fc458cfbe1d7f2c85638c6165b636), (https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/59452.diff)).
**Affects:** Applications that have duplicate code after running the `ng update @angular/core@20` migration for unused imports.
**Action:** required: Revert the duplicate code introduced by the buggy `cleanup-unused-imports` migration and re-verify that no duplication occurs when the migration is applied. Alternatively, run the `ng g @angular/core:cleanup-unused-imports` schematic manually after updating to 20 (https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/cleanup-unused-imports).

**Before/after:**
```typescript
// Before (buggy schematic code)
recorder
  .remove(c.data.position, c.data.end - c.data.position)
  .insertLeft(c.data.position, c.data.toInsert);

// After (fixed schematic code)
recorder
  .remove(c.data.position, c.data.end - c.data.position)
  .insertRight(c.data.position, c.data.toInsert);
```

**What changed:** During Hot Module Replacement (HMR), `@angular/animations` schedules destruction of its animation renderer *after* currently-running animations finish; when no animations were running, the renderer was only destroyed "next time around", so stale component styles could remain in the DOM for a long time and leak into the replaced component. Angular 20 fixes this by (1) moving the renderer cleanup to after the destruction of the old view, so the usual cleanup flow has been kicked off, and (2) flushing animations when a component is replaced, using `AnimationEngine.flush()` (`this._transitionEngine.flush(microtaskId)`), so the renderer is destroyed promptly (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59574, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a4eb74c79cca802d8179118cf4d53c73285baadb). It builds on the related fix "destroy renderer when replacing styles during HMR", where the renderer was previously removed from the cache but never had `destroy` called on it (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/59514). Internally this relies on `AnimationEngine.destroy(namespaceId, context)` and `AnimationEngine.flush()` in `packages/animations/browser/src/render/animation_engine_next.ts`.

**Affects:** Applications using `@angular/animations` (animations module / `trigger`-based animations) together with HMR (`ng serve --hmr`) in development; behaviour of animation style removal timing during view teardown. No production API surface changed.

**Action:** none — this is an internal bug fix. Only re-verify that component styles are removed correctly after an HMR swap of an animated component, and that no tests assert on previously-leaked animation styles persisting in the DOM.

**What changed:** Angular's HMR engine (`packages/core/src/render3/hmr.ts`, used by the internal `ɵɵreplaceMetadata` / `ɵɵgetReplaceMetadataURL` codeGen APIs) previously failed to find and replace live component instances when the component injects `ViewContainerRef`. In that case the component's `LView` is wrapped in an empty `LContainer` whose `HOST` slot is the `LView`, and the recursive `recreateMatchingLViews` traversal only walked `LContainer` entries from `CONTAINER_HEADER_OFFSET`, so such components were never matched against `oldDef.tView` and their templates were not live-reloaded (issue #59592, regression reported against 19.x). The fix adds, inside `recreateMatchingLViews`, a check that recurses into `current[HOST]` when `isLContainer(current)` and `isLView(current[HOST])` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/6f7716268afa5146f2b2d0dbbea146defa9acfef, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59596, https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.0.0/packages/core/src/render3/hmr.ts).

**Affects:** Applications using Angular HMR (`ng serve --hmr`) with components that inject `ViewContainerRef` (e.g. `vcr = inject(ViewContainerRef)`); purely a dev-server/HMR correctness fix, no production behaviour or public API change.

**Action:** none — the fix is internal to `@angular/core`; no application code, template, or build configuration changes are required. Re-verify that editing the template of a component that injects `ViewContainerRef` triggers in-place HMR replacement instead of a full page reload.

*No before/after snippet is shown: the only code differing between versions is internal framework source (`packages/core/src/render3/hmr.ts`), not application code or configuration.*

**What changed:** This is an internal bug fix to the `cleanup-unused-imports` migration in `packages/core/schematics/ng-generate/cleanup-unused-imports/unused_imports_migration.ts` (the schematic run via `ng generate @angular/core:cleanup-unused-imports`, which removes symbols from `@Component.imports` that aren't used in a template and reported as of Angular 19) (https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/cleanup-unused-imports). When a file belonged to multiple TypeScript programs, the migration counted it twice, so the printed statistics (e.g. "Removed 2 imports in 1 file") were wrong, even though the actual string replacements were applied correctly. The fix de-duplicates at merge time in `combineCompilationUnits`: replacements are keyed by `getReplacementID()` (`projectFile.id + '/' + position + '/' + end + '/' + toInsert`), and the `removedImports` counter in `CompilationUnitData` was replaced by a `removedIdentifiers: NodeID[]` list whose length feeds `stats()`; `changedFiles` is now the size of a `Set<ProjectFileID>` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a62c84bc188d41ea24cf0eca14ac18c4b917ccd0).

**Affects:** Only the migration schematic's console statistics output, mainly in projects where files appear in multiple tsconfig programs; no application code is affected.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```diff
-      removedImports: unitA.removedImports + unitB.removedImports,
-      changedFiles: unitA.changedFiles + unitB.changedFiles,
+      replacements: combinedReplacements,
+      removedIdentifiers: combinedRemovedIdentifiers,
+      changedFiles: changedFileIds.size,
```

**What changed:** The Angular 20.0.0 `@angular/platform-browser` package updates the pseudoevent created by `createMouseSpecialEvent` (part of the HammerJS gesture plugin) to now populate the `_originalEvent` property, which previously was not set. This fixes an internal bug and is explicitly marked as not introducing a breaking change (<https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59690>). The fix landed as a patch, e.g. commit `12256574626f04f5fe2b41e805f7bdc93d62df0a` (<https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/12256574626f04f5fe2b41e805f7bdc93d62df0a>).

**Affects:** Applications using the HammerJS gesture integration in `@angular/platform-browser` that observe gesture pseudoevents built via `createMouseSpecialEvent` and inspect the `_originalEvent` property.

**Action:** none — the change is an internal bug fix that populates `_originalEvent`; applications need not change code, configuration, dependencies, build, or deployment. The PR does not add tests or document user-facing behavior (<https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59690>). No concrete code/configuration snippet for the before/after form is available from the fetched pages.

**What changed:** Angular 20 integrates angular/angular-cli#29510 into the core HMR runtime. Previously, when a component hot-reload replacement failed at runtime, the erroneous component update stayed applied in the dev server's HMR data. Now, if the replacement throws an error, the client signals the dev server, which clears the errant component update and triggers a full page reload; the action is logged to the dev server console with an optional message from the client (https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/pull/29510, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59854, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/cab7a9b69c3a5d789432a87a554e8489c78a0f15). A companion change in the same PR, `refactor(compiler): pass more information to HMR replacement function`, adjusts generated HMR code to pass the HMR ID and `import.meta` to the `replaceMetadata` call, to enable better error logging (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59854). Both were `action: merge`, `target: patch` changes merged for the 20.0.0 release.

**Affects:** Applications using the `@angular/build` development server with HMR enabled (component hot reload). Internal/generated HMR code only; not application-written code.

**Action:** none — this is an internal dev-server/runtime reliability fix. Teams with custom HMR `replaceMetadata` replacement functions should re-verify that HMR error handling still behaves as expected after upgrading.

**What changed:** `throwInvalidWriteToSignalError` now takes the signal node in question and passes it to the `throwInvalidWriteToSignalErrorFn` handler function, so the handler can include details such as the signal name in the error message (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59600, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/2588985f433b20a6a5a8d239347291f5d6fb2451). The PR explicitly marks this as a non-breaking feature, with the current behavior previously being a zero-argument call and the new behavior passing the signal node.

**Affects:** Applications that register a custom signal-write error handler via `throwInvalidWriteToSignalErrorFn` (the internal handler consumed by `throwInvalidWriteToSignalError`). Normal applications that only use `signal()`/`computed()`/`linkedSignal()` without overriding this handler are unaffected.

**Action:** none. The PR declares the change non-breaking; a handler written for the old zero-argument signature keeps working because it simply ignores the extra argument. If you have a custom handler that inspects error arguments, re-verify that it still behaves as expected with the added signal node. No migration step is specified in the sources.

**What changed:** Angular v19 supported TypeScript 5.4–5.7; Angular 20.0.0 added TypeScript 5.8 support via `feat(core): support TypeScript 5.8 (#59830)` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59830, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/146ab9a76e6b4d8db7d08d34e2571ba5207f8756). The `@angular/build` 20.0.0 release notes list as a breaking change that "TypeScript versions less than 5.8 are no longer supported", and Angular 20 requires the `typescript` peer dependency at `>=5.8.0 <5.9.0` (https://github.com/angular/angular-cli/releases/tag/20.0.0, ).

**Affects:** All Angular applications and libraries upgrading to v20 that currently pin `typescript` below `5.8.0`, or that pin it to `>=5.9.0` (the upper bound `<5.9.0` excludes TS 5.9+).

**Action:** required: update the `devDependencies.typescript` value in `package.json` to a version satisfying `>=5.8.0 <5.9.0` before running `ng update`; then re-verify that the project compiles cleanly under TypeScript 5.8 (TS 5.8 introduces stricter checks such as the `URL` / `Map` type-relationship changes, so new type errors may surface).

**Before/after:**
```json
// package.json (devDependencies)
-    "typescript": "~5.6.0"
+    "typescript": "~5.8.0"
```

**What changed:** PR #58250 was reverted in #59455 (PR #59551), then reapplied in #59551 for Angular 20.0.0. The applied change (#58250) makes `afterRender`/`afterNextRender` calls associated with a particular view not register until after the first time the view is rendered (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/58250, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59551). The reapplication #59551 is titled "Reapply 'fix(core): Defer afterRender until after first CD (#58250)'" and states: "For `afterRender`/`afterNextRender` calls associated with a particular view, ensure that they are not registered until after the first time the view is rendered." (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/59551)

**Affects:** Applications using `afterRender` or `afterNextRender` callbacks that are associated with a specific view/component and expect them to fire before the first change-detection/render pass for that view.

**Action:** none

**What changed:** Angular 20 adds a schematic to convert component selectors in templates from separate opening and closing tags to self-closing tags (https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/self-closing-tags). The PR states the change is "purely aesthetic" and does not affect application behavior (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/1cd3a7db83e1d05a31d23324676420b614cdabe2). Self-closing tag support originally shipped in v16 (https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/self-closing-tags). The `self-closing-tags-migration` schematic is registered with alias `self-closing-tag` in `@angular/core` schematics collection (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/main/packages/core/schematics/collection.json).

**Affects:** Applications that want to modernize template syntax to use self-closing tags. The migration is optional and does not affect runtime behavior.

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```html
<!-- Before -->
<app-home hello="world"></app-home>

<!-- After -->
<app-home hello="world" />
```
(https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/main/packages/core/schematics/ng-generate/self-closing-tags-migration/README.md)

**What changed:** Angular 20 automatically disables browser animations on the server by checking `ngServerMode`, removing the need for an explicit import of the animations module in server-side applications. Additionally, the hard dependency between `platform-server` and `platform-browser/animations` has been removed, meaning `platform-server` no longer implicitly imports or depends on `@angular/platform-browser/animations`.
Affects: Applications using `platform-server` (Angular Universal SSR) with animations.
Action: required: Verify that animations are correctly disabled during server-side rendering if you previously relied on importing `NoopAnimationsModule` or `BrowserAnimationsModule` explicitly. If `platform-server` previously included animations via a hidden dependency and you relied on specific behavior, verify that behavior remains correct or update code to no longer expect animations to be active during SSR.
**Before/after:**
```
<!-- In platform-server context, no need for explicit animation module import if previously relying on implicit inclusion -->
```

**What changed:** This is a bug fix in `@angular/compiler-cli` for the generation of Hot Module Replacement (HMR) code. The `compiler-cli` previously retrieved the source file of a class by calling `node.getSourceFile()` directly on the transformed TypeScript AST node (e.g., in `extractHmrMetatadata`, `extractHmrDependencies`, and `getHmrUpdateDeclaration`). If the class was transformed by a custom TypeScript transformer, `node.getSourceFile()` would fail or return undefined, causing `ng serve` to crash with a `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'fileName')` at `extractHmrMetatadata`. The fix retrieves the source file from the original node via `ts.getOriginalNode(node).getSourceFile()` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60298, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/60287). The fix was released in patch `19.2.12`, so an application upgrading directly to `20.0.0` receives this fix and the HMR `TypeError` no longer occurs.

**Affects:** applications with enabled HMR (e.g. `serve` target with `"liveReload": false, "hmr": true` in `angular.json`) and custom TypeScript transformers that transform `@Component` classes (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/60287).

**Action:** none

**What changed:** The `@angular/platform-server` package imports from `rxjs`, but `rxjs` was not declared in its `peerDependencies` (nor `dependencies`). This missing declaration surfaced as errors in strict dependency environments, such as pnpm's symlinked `node_modules` structure (it typically did not fail with Yarn or npm because of node_modules hoisting). PR #60308 added `"rxjs": "^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0"` to the `peerDependencies` of `packages/platform-server/package.json` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/15c42969fc42c76e3bd593201164183fb82d70f6.patch, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60308).

**Affects:** Applications using `@angular/platform-server` (SSR) installed with strict package managers such as pnpm, where an undeclared `rxjs` import previously produced resolution/module-not-found errors; also apps pinned to an `rxjs` version outside `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0` (practically, older rxjs 6.x).

**Action:** required: re-verify that `rxjs` (matching `^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0`) is installed and resolvable alongside `@angular/platform-server` after upgrading, particularly in pnpm workspaces — the new peerDependency makes npm/pnpm warn or error if it is missing or mismatched. No application code changes are needed.

**Before/after:**
```json
// packages/platform-server/package.json — peerDependencies
-    "@angular/platform-browser": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER"
+    "@angular/platform-browser": "0.0.0-PLACEHOLDER",
+    "rxjs": "^6.5.3 || ^7.4.0"
```

**What changed:** This commit is internal test-infra bookkeeping only. It changes one line in `packages/core/test/bundling/router/bundle.golden_symbols.json`, renaming the expected bundled symbol `stringify12` to `stringify13` (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/7bcdf7c1435f766b2b0bbd383358ef2ddabf217a.patch). PR #60233 is labeled `action: merge, area: router, target: patch`, and its "Does this PR introduce a breaking change?" box is checked **No** (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60233). The goldens in that directory were unchanged on the 19.2.x line, where the file still lists `stringify12` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/19.2.x/packages/core/test/bundling/router/bundle.golden_symbols.json). The renamed symbol is a private, mangled local in the bundling golden list, not any public `@angular/router` export (the golden's public entries remain things like `Router`, `RouterLink`, `UrlTree`). It belongs under "internal fixes", not breaking changes, despite the row's Breaking Changes section hint.

**Affects:** none — no application, library, or build configuration references `bundle.golden_symbols.json` or the mangled symbol `stringify12`/`stringify13`.

**Action:** none

**What changed:** Angular's SSR hydration content-integrity check was made tolerant of valid HTML5 documents that omit the `<body>` (and/or `<head>`) tag. Before the fix, the internal `verifySsrContentsIntegrity()` in `packages/core/src/hydration/api.ts` searched only `doc.body.childNodes` for the comment marker `nghm` (`SSR_CONTENT_INTEGRITY_MARKER`) and threw a `RuntimeError` with `RuntimeErrorCode.MISSING_SSR_CONTENT_INTEGRITY_MARKER` (`NG0507`) when it was not found (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60429, https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/60429.diff). The function was moved to `packages/core/src/hydration/utils.ts` as `export function verifySsrContentsIntegrity(doc: Document): void`, and now, after scanning `doc.body.childNodes`, also checks `doc.body.previousSibling` (`skipTextNodes`) and `doc.head.lastChild` (`skipTextNodes`) so a marker the HTML parser relocated to before the implicit `<body>` or at the end of an implicit `<head>` is accepted (https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/60429.diff). `NG0507` maps to `MISSING_SSR_CONTENT_INTEGRITY_MARKER = -507` (https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/13a8709b2ba29ef3ab7d38bfb41cdd3d44c24c51/packages/core/src/errors.ts). Motivation: allow more HTML minification and easier integration with systems composing response fragments from different sources (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60429).
**Affects:** Applications using client-side hydration (`provideClientHydration()`) with SSR, where the served document omits an explicit `<body>` (and/or `<head>`) tag so the browser relocates the `nghm` integrity marker outside `<body>`.
**Action:** none: applications no longer need to keep an explicit `<body>` tag solely to avoid the `NG0507` `MISSING_SSR_CONTENT_INTEGRITY_MARKER` error, but hydration must be re-verified when the response omits `<body>`/`<head>` or is minified by a CDN or build step.
**Before/after:**
```html
<!doctype html><head><title>Hi</title></head><!--nghm--><app-root></app-root>
```
https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/60429.diff

**What changed:** The control-flow migration schematic (`ng generate @angular/core:control-flow`) previously failed to delete `ng-template` definitions that were used via `else` or referenced elsewhere (for example `*ngTemplateOutlet`), leaving unused template declarations in the migrated template. The internal search/counting logic in the schematic changed from a regex-based match to an AST-based `countTemplateUsage` that handles `@for`, `*ngTemplateOutlet`, and `if-else` references so the now-unused `ng-template` (for example `#loading` from `*ngIf="param; else loading"`) is removed. The PR replaces the regex `escapeRegExp` counting in `packages/core/schematics/ng-generate/control-flow-migration/util.ts` with AST traversal in `getTemplates`/`countTemplateUsage`/`processNgTemplates`. (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60459, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/081f5f5a83fef99718952519bed9fe39005d6d37, https://patch-diff.githubusercontent.com/raw/angular/angular/pull/60459.diff, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/56965) **Affects:** Applications that run the control-flow migration schematic (`ng generate @angular/core:control-flow`) on templates containing `ng-template` blocks referenced via `else` (for example `*ngIf="param; else loading"`), `*ngTemplateOutlet`, or `@for`; it is a bug fix in the migration tool, not a runtime change, and is marked as a non-breaking patch. (https://angular.dev/reference/migrations/control-flow, https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60459) **Action:** required: re-verify the output of the control-flow migration — confirm that `ng-template` blocks that were previously left behind after `*ngIf="…; else …"`, `*ngTemplateOutlet`, or `@for` references are now correctly deleted in the migrated templates, and that no still-referenced `ng-template` was inadvertently removed. (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60459) **Before/after:** ``` // comp.html input to the control-flow migration
content
loading
 // After migration: the block is expected to be removed ```

**What changed:** The `ng add @angular/localize` schematic (`packages/localize/schematics/ng-add/index.ts`) previously skipped projects whose test target uses the new `@angular/build:karma` builder, so the `@angular/localize/init` polyfill was never added to the Karma test configuration — a problem because Angular CLI v20 generates new applications with `@angular/build:karma` as the default test builder (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60513). The fix adds `case AngularBuilder.BuildKarma:` alongside `AngularBuilder.Karma` in `addPolyfillToConfig`, so the schematic now appends `'@angular/localize/init'` to the target's `options.polyfills` (converting a string value like `'zone.js'` to `['zone.js', '@angular/localize/init']`) for `@angular/build:karma` targets, and also in the tsconfig `types` handling (`addTypeScriptConfigTypes` adds `@angular/localize` to `compilerOptions.types` of the target's `tsConfig`) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/a2f622d82d6c0f93a5fdf34fc8e5829db04c7380.patch).

**Affects:** Applications that run `ng add @angular/localize` on Angular 20 projects where the `test` target uses the `@angular/build:karma` builder; existing projects already migrated with older versions may be missing the polyfill in the karma builder's `polyfills`. Not a breaking change (PR: "Does this PR introduce a breaking change? No").

**Action:** none — no code or configuration must change on upgrade; only the schematic's behaviour is fixed. Applications that ran `ng add @angular/localize` under Angular CLI v20 before this fix should re-verify that `@angular/localize/init` is present in the `polyfills` of the `@angular/build:karma` test target in `angular.json`.

**Before/after:**
```diff
       switch (target.builder) {
         case AngularBuilder.Karma:
+        case AngularBuilder.BuildKarma:
         case AngularBuilder.Server:
         case AngularBuilder.Browser:
         case AngularBuilder.BrowserEsbuild:
```

**What changed:** The Angular `compiler-cli`'s `NgCompiler` (in `packages/compiler-cli/src/ngtsc/core/src/compiler.ts`) previously selected the `LogicalProjectStrategy` for in-project relative imports whenever a TypeScript `rootDir` **or** `rootDirs` option was set. `rootDirs` (virtual directory support) is not the same as `rootDir`, and entering `LogicalProjectStrategy` mode on a plain `rootDir` broke monorepo builds where generated imports point outside the `rootDir` — e.g. to another compilation unit's `.d.ts` file, which is valid (only `.ts` sources must live inside the root dir). v20 narrowed the condition to `this.options.rootDirs !== undefined && this.options.rootDirs.length > 0`, so `LogicalProjectStrategy` is now only used when `rootDirs` is set; with just `rootDir`, plain relative imports are used and symbols outside `rootDir` (such as `../lib/dir.d.ts` declarations) can be imported without compiler diagnostics (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60555, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/22a0e54ac4ae7b943740dc314ff7f26ee7530ee5). This was noted as necessary for Angular's Bazel toolchain migration and shipped as a fix, not listed as a breaking change in the v20.0.0 release notes (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/20.0.0).

**Affects:** Applications/libraries compiled by `@angular/compiler-cli` that set `rootDir` (but not `rootDirs`) in `tsconfig.json` and reference symbols whose declarations (`.d.ts`) live outside `rootDir` — typical in monorepos and Bazel-style builds.

**Action:** none — this is a bug fix restoring correct behavior; projects previously broken by this issue now compile. Projects relying on the old accidental behavior should re-verify that generated relative imports still resolve.

I have the sources but no official v20 update-guide page confirming this fix is in 20.0.x, and the commit page does not show version tags. The change is a compiler-cli patch fixing defer dependency generation for pipes. I will present only what the commit patch supports.

**What changed:** The `@Component` compiler handler previously called `extractPipes(dependencies)` using only the component's standard `dependencies`, so pipes that appeared in a component's `deferredImports` were missing from the `pipes` map. The handler now calls `extractPipes(allDependencies)` where `allDependencies = [...explicitlyDeferredDependencies, ...dependencies]` (built when `@Component.deferredImports` is non-empty), and when scanning defer-block `BoundTarget`s it now uses `bound.getUsedDirectives()` and `bound.getUsedPipes()` instead of the previously used `bound.getEagerlyUsedDirectives()` and `bound.getEagerlyUsedPipes()`; this includes pipes used anywhere in a defer block, so deferred pipes are no longer omitted from defer dependency generation and instead appear in generated `ɵɵdefer(...)` dependency functions and `ɵsetClassMetadataAsync` dynamic imports (for example `import("./pipe-a").then(m => m.PipeA)`). The PR marks this as not a breaking change (`area: core`, `target: patch`). (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/60571)

**Affects:** Standalone components that declare pipes via `deferredImports` and use them inside `@defer` blocks, which under v19 omitted those pipes from the generated defer dependency metadata.

**Action:** none — the compiler is now fixed to include deferred pipes; no code or configuration changes are required, but the defer-block pipe rendering should be re-verified after recompiling.

**Before/after:**
```js
// before fix (deferred pipe omitted from defer dependency function):
'const AppCmp_Defer_1_DepsFn = () => [' +
  'import("./deferred-a").then(m => m.DeferredCmpA)];',

// after fix (deferred PipeA now included):
'const AppCmp_For_1_Conditional_0_Defer_1_DepsFn = () => [' +
  'import("./deferred-a").then(m => m.DeferredCmpA), ' +
  'import("./pipe-a").then(m => m.PipeA)];',
```

**What changed:** This change fixes a bug where the runtime threw a DI error (`NullInjectorError`, `Error: NG0200`) when attempting to inject a missing `useExisting` provider via `inject(Token, { optional: true })`. In Angular 19, if a provider used `useExisting` to refer to another, unavailable `ProviderToken`, `inject` with the `{ optional: true }` flag would throw instead of returning `null`. The root cause was that `useExisting` triggered a secondary internal `inject` call that failed to propagate the `InjectFlags` (like `Optional`) from the original call. The fix ensures the flags from the original call are included in the second `inject` call. (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/61152, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/61121, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/4623b6144897c6063139afa2d189be4e2e1d70ba)

**Affects:** Applications using `inject()` or `@Optional()` on `useExisting` providers where the aliased provider is potentially missing. (https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/61121)

**Action:** none

**Before/after:**
```typescript
// Before (Angular 19 - threw NullInjectorError if aliased provider missing)
const value = inject(MissingToken, { optional: true });
```

**What changed:** Before Angular 20, the compiler generated the HMR replacement URL inline in each component's compiled output as `new URL("./@ng/component?c=" + id + "&t=" + encodeURIComponent(t), import.meta.url).href`. If application code declared a local symbol named `URL` (e.g. `export enum URL { MY = 'MY' }`), the generated code shadowed the native constructor and the dev server app failed at runtime with `Uncaught TypeError: URL is not a constructor` (regression vs v18, reported in #61517) (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/44bb328eaea028524206d0d2b9f12702c9bf3861, https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/61517). Angular 20 moves URL construction into a new private core function `ɵɵgetReplaceMetadataURL(id: string, timestamp: string, base: string): string` in `packages/core/src/render3/hmr.ts`, exported from `@angular/core`'s render3 private exports and registered in `angularCoreEnv`; the generated HMR code now emits `i0.ɵɵgetReplaceMetadataURL(id, t, import.meta.url)` instead of the inline `new URL(...)` expression, resolved by the compiler via `R3.getReplaceMetadataURL` in `r3_identifiers.ts` / `r3_hmr_compiler.ts` (https://github.com/angular/angular/pull/61550, https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/44bb328eaea028524206d0d2b9f12702c9bf3861). This is a compiler-internal fix; it is listed only as a fix in the 20.0.0 release notes, not under Breaking Changes (https://github.com/angular/angular/releases/tag/20.0.0).

**Affects:** Applications using the dev-server HMR feature (`hmr` option, enabled by default in the esbuild/Vite builder) that declare a local symbol named `URL` — this previously broke `ng serve` at runtime.

**Action:** none — the fix is applied automatically by the v20 compiler; no code, config, or dependency changes are needed. Applications previously working around the bug (renaming the `URL` symbol or setting `hmr: false`) can revert the workaround, and `ng serve` HMR behavior can be re-verified.

**Before/after:**
```diff
-// new URL(urlValue, urlBase).href
-const urlHref = new o.InstantiateExpr(o.variable('URL'), [urlValue, urlBase]).prop('href');
+// getReplaceMetadataURL(id, timestamp, import.meta.url)
+const url = o
+  .importExpr(R3.getReplaceMetadataURL)
+  .callFn([
+    o.variable(idName),
+    o.variable(timestampName),
+    o.variable('import').prop('meta').prop('url'),
+  ]);
```

**What changed:** The fetched pages did not document a change where Angular "only applies known attributes from HTML in translated ICU content" for the 19.0.0 → 20.0.0 hop. The `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/angular/angular/20.0.0/CHANGELOG.md` lists several behavioral breaking changes under `compiler` (`in` operator, `void` operator) and `core`/`router` (e.g., `ApplicationRef.tick`, `RedirectFn`, `Route` guards), but not the ICU attribute dropping mentioned in the title. The `https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-prjf-86w9-mfqv` page describes an XSS vulnerability (CVE-2026-27970) fixed in patched versions (e.g., 20.3.17, 19.2.19) due to improper sanitization of HTML attributes in translated ICU messages, which is a subsequent bug fix patch, not a breaking change in v20.0.0.

**Affects:** N/A

**Action:** N/A

**What changed:** Angular 20.0.0 changes how attributes are processed within translated ICU messages. Previously, any attribute present in the translated HTML (except those on a blocklist of sensitive URI attributes like `href`/`src`, which were just sanitized) was applied to the DOM. Now, Angular uses an allowlist: only known valid attributes (e.g., `class`) are applied, and if a known URI attribute (like `href`) appears with a static value from a translation, its value is replaced with `'unsafe:blocked'` to prevent malicious link creation. Any other unknown attribute (e.g., `label`, `attr`) is dropped entirely and not rendered (, ). **Affects:** Applications using internationalization (i18n) where translated ICU messages contain HTML elements with attributes. Specifically, any attributes that are not in Angular's internal allowlist will now be silently removed from the rendered output. **Action:** required: Audit translation files (e.g., XLIFF) for ICU messages containing HTML with non-standard or non-allowlisted attributes. If such attributes are used for functionality (not just semantics), refactor to move these attributes into the component template or use supported Angular binding syntax instead. **Before/after:** ```html
{count, plural, =1 {Item} }
```

**What changed:** The Angular compiler added 'iframe|src' to the TRUSTED_TYPES_SINKS set in packages/compiler/src/schema/trusted_types_sinks.ts (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5be912eb55fe88e8621e2ce82470d51b7d950ceb). This set defines attributes that are Trusted Types sinks; previously 'iframe|src' was absent, so the compiler permitted i18n-attribute bindings on an iframe's src without the sanitization / Trusted Types requirements applied to other sinks such as 'embed|src', 'object|data', 'iframe|srcdoc' and 'iframe|src'. As a result, internationalized src values on iframes could bypass sanitization, which is a security issue (CVE-2026-32635: an i18n-<attribute> combined with a data binding to untrusted data on a security-sensitive attribute like href/src bypassed Angular's built-in sanitization and could inject a malicious URL / javascript: URL into the DOM) (https://www.miggo.io/vulnerability-database/cve/CVE-2026-32635). The commit also updated the source-spec link from  to  and added the isTrustedTypesSink('iframe', 'src') === true case to trusted_types_sinks_spec.ts (https://github.com/angular/angular/commit/5be912eb55fe88e8621e2ce82470d51b7d950ceb).

**Affects:** Applications that mark the src attribute of an <iframe> for translation using i18n-src (or the equivalent i18n attribute syntax) while binding it to a value, i.e. applications relying on translated / data-bound iframe src values being handled without Trusted Types enforcement.

**Action:** required: Re-verify any <iframe> element whose src attribute is translated with i18n-src (or i18n attribute on src) and bound to dynamic data. src on iframe is now a Trusted Types sink, so values supplied through the i18n attribute must satisfy Trusted Types (RESOURCE_URL / TrustedScriptURL handling via ElementSchemaRegistry.securityContext) rather than being written raw; confirm translated URLs still render as expected.

**Before/after:**
```ts
// before (trusted_types_sinks.ts)
const TRUSTED_TYPES_SINKS = new Set<string>([
  'iframe|srcdoc',
  '*|innerhtml',
  '*|outerhtml',
  'embed|src',
  'object|codebase',
  'object|data',
]);

// after (trusted_types_sinks.ts)
const TRUSTED_TYPES_SINKS = new Set<string>([
  'iframe|srcdoc',
  '*|innerhtml',
  '*|outerhtml',
  'embed|src',
  'iframe|src',
  'object|codebase',
  'object|data',
]);
